mgmt_bio.text: Sundar Pichai, 53, is chief executive officer of Alphabet Inc. and Google and has served as a director of Alphabet since 2017, having joined Google in 2004 and been named CEO of Google in October 2015 and of Alphabet in December 2019. He previously served as Google's Senior Vice President of Products from October 2014 to October 2015 and as Senior Vice President of Android, Chrome and Apps from March 2013 to October 2014. He has led product and engineering for Google's products and platforms, including Search, Chrome, Maps, Android, Gmail and Google Workspace, and as CEO has shifted company strategy toward AI.

citations.title: Alphabet earnings call Q2 2026: Sundar Pichai remarks

sentences.quote:
Alphabet revenue grew 24% year-over-year. Our AI investments are redefining what's possible across every part of our business.
Our momentum starts with Search
sentences.text: Public filings show execution under Sundar Pichai centred on AI: Alphabet revenue grew 24% year over year in Q2 2026, with Search and Other up 17%.

Capital allocation has swung toward AI infrastructure: 2026 capex is guided to $180-190 billion, with 2027 expected to rise significantly, funded partly by an $80 billion equity raise announced in June 2026, including a $10 billion Berkshire Hathaway private placement, while no Class A or C shares were repurchased in Q1 2026 and the dividend rose 5% to $0.22.
Governance is founder-controlled: Larry Page and Sergey Brin held about 52.7% of voting power as of April 6, 2026, which the company says severely restricts other stockholders' influence.

citations.title: Alphabet Q2 2026: Search Ads Grew 17% in AI Overviews Era

sentences.quote: Google Search and other advertising revenues increased by 17% to $63.3 billion, with retail and finance driving the largest contributions.
sentences.text: Alphabet's core Google Search and other advertising remains the engine, with revenue up 17% to $63.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026, led by retail and finance, as users adopt AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search.
Google Cloud is the second growth pillar: revenue rose 82% to $24.8 billion, while cloud operating income more than tripled to $8.8 billion and margin widened from 20.7% to 35.6%.
Cloud backlog reached $514 billion, up more than $50 billion sequentially, with just over 50% expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 24 months, supporting revenue visibility.
Recurring consumer revenue is scaling, as Google reached 350 million paid subscriptions, with the first quarter of 2026 its strongest ever for consumer AI plans.

sentences.quote: Capital expenditures hit $44.9 billion in the quarter - roughly double the $22.4 billion of Q2 2025 - and Alphabet raised full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195-205 billion
sentences.text: The main offset is capital intensity: capex doubled to $44.9 billion and full-year guidance was raised to $195-205 billion.
